questions.question: Chad Sukra festival is celebrated by the Jaintia tribe of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Chad Sukra festival** is celebrated by the **Jaintia tribe of Meghalaya, **also known as the **Pnar people, every year in April.**
 
• The festival honors the start of the sowing season and is also a way to ask for protection from natural calamities that could harm crops.
 
• The festival dates back to the **Jaintia Kingdom**, when the king would move his court from **Sutnga to Jaintiapur,** and people from all over the kingdom would perform for him and his ministers at the start of spring.
 
• The word Chad Sukra literally means "dance with a joyful heart, with health and vitality".
 
• During the festival, farmers offer prayers to mother earth and thank her for her blessings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In addition to rituals and prayers, the Chad Sukra festival features traditional dances, including the **"Laho" dance.**
 
• In this dance, two young men flank a girl, linking arms with her, and they dance together in synchronized steps.
 
• Women participating in the festival adorn themselves in traditional attire such as ryndia stem, thoh saru, khyrwang, sapjat, kein shrooh/kyrshah, while men wear iuslein pyniein, iuspong, ryndia tlem, among others.
 
• Furthermore, women embellish their attire with ornaments like paila, khoila (earrings), and khadu (bracelets), adding to the festive atmosphere of the occasion.

questions.question: Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. It is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of the monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. **

 
 
• **It is celebrated in Odisha**.
 
• The second day of the festival signifies the beginning of the solar month of Mithuna, during which the season of rains starts.
 
• It falls in mid-June, the first day is called Pahili Raja, the second day is Mithuna Sankranti, the third day is Bhudaaha or Basi Raja.
 
• The final fourth day is called Basumati snana, in which the ladies bathe the grinding stone as a symbol of Bhumi with turmeric paste and adore with flower, sindoor, etc.
 
• All types of seasonal fruits are offered to** mother Bhumi**.
 
• The day before the first day is called Sajabaja or preparatory day during which the house, kitchen including grinding stones are cleaned, spices are ground for three days.
 
• During these three days, women and girls take a rest from work and wear new Saree, Alata, and ornaments.
 
• It is similar to **Ambubachi Mela**.
 
• It is believed that the mother Goddess Earth or the divine wife of Lord Vishnu undergoes menstruation during the first three days.
 
• The fourth day is called Vasumati Snana, or the ceremonial bath of Bhudevi.
 
• The term Raja came from the Sanskrit word 'Rajas' which means menstruation and when a woman menstruates, she is called 'Rajaswala' or a menstruating woman, and in medieval times the festival became more popular as an agricultural holiday marking the worship of Bhudevi, who is the wife of Lord Jagannath.
 
• A silver idol of **Bhudevi **is still to be found in the Puri Temple beside Lord Jagannath.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Magha Bihu: In Assam and many parts of the North East, the festival of Magha Bihu is celebrated. It sees the first harvest of the season is offered to the gods along with prayers for peace and prosperity.
 
• Uttarayan: Gujarat celebrates it in the form of the convivial kite festival of Uttarayan.
 
• Maghi: In Punjab, Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Maghi. Bathing in a river in the early hours of Maghi is important.
 
• Saaji: In the Shimla District of Himachal Pradesh, Makara Sankranti is known as Magha Saaji. Saaji is the Pahari word for Sankranti, the start of the new month. Hence this day marks the start of the month of Magha.

questions.question: Which festival was initiated by Shivaji, in his reign, to channalise the patriotic spirit of Hindus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganesh Chaturthi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Ganesh Chaturthi is an annual Hindu festival that celebrates the birth of Ganesha, the elephant-headed god.
 
• The festival was popularized by Shivaji Maharaj, the great Maratha ruler, in the 17th century to promote culture and nationalism.
 
• The celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi was revived by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in the late 19th century to unite Indians against British rule.
 
• The festival involves the installation of Ganesha idols in homes and public places, followed by prayers, cultural performances, and processions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shivaji Maharaj:**

 
 
• Shivaji Maharaj, also known as Chhatrapati Shivaji, was the founder of the Maratha Empire in western India.
 
• He established a competent and progressive civil rule with well-structured administrative organizations.
 
• Shivaji is known for his innovative military tactics, guerrilla warfare, and strong naval presence.
 
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:**
 
 
• Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indian nationalist, teacher, and independence activist.
 
• He was one of the first leaders of the Indian Independence Movement and is often referred to as "Lokmanya," which means "accepted by the people."
 
• Tilak revived the celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi to build a sense of unity and nationalism among Indians during British rule.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Chaturthi Celebrations:**
 
 
• The festival typically lasts for 10 days, starting on the fourth day of the Hindu lunar calendar month of Bhadrapada.
 
• Activities include the installation of Ganesha idols, prayers (aartis), cultural performances, and community feasts.
 
• On the final day, known as Anant Chaturdashi, the idols are paraded through the streets and immersed in water bodies in a ritual called Visarjan.

questions.question: "Dashain" and "Tihar" are popular festivals of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Dashain** and **Tihar** are the two most significant festivals celebrated in **Nepal**, marking cultural and religious importance in the country.
 
• Dashain, also known as **Vijaya Dashami**, symbolizes the victory of good over evil and is dedicated to the Goddess Durga.
 
• Tihar, also called the **Festival of Lights**, is a five-day celebration that honors various animals, brothers, and the Goddess Laxmi, the deity of wealth.
 
• Both festivals are widely celebrated by the **Hindu majority population** of Nepal, and they reflect Nepal's rich cultural heritage.
 
• Dashain typically falls in September-October, while Tihar occurs in October-November, based on the lunar calendar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dashain:**

 
 
• Dashain is observed for 15 days, with each day representing different rituals, including **Ghatasthapana**, **Phulpati**, and **Vijaya Dashami**.
 
• It signifies the victory of Goddess Durga over the demon **Mahishasura**.
 
• The festival is marked by family gatherings, animal sacrifices, and the receiving of **Tika (rice, yogurt, and vermilion)** from elders.
 
• It is a time for new clothes, feasts, and the renewal of family and community bonds.
 
 
 
• **Tihar:**
 
 
• Also known as **Yama Panchak**, Tihar honors animals like crows, dogs, and cows, recognizing their role in human life.
 
• The third day, **Laxmi Puja**, is the most celebrated, with people lighting oil lamps and decorating homes to welcome the Goddess of Wealth.
 
• The fifth day, known as **Bhai Tika**, strengthens the bond between brothers and sisters through rituals and gift exchanges.
 
 
 
• **Religious and Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Both festivals are rooted in **Hindu mythology**, with Dashain focusing on divine power and Tihar emphasizing familial and animal respect.
 
• They are also celebrated among Nepalese communities worldwide, showcasing Nepal's cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Public Celebrations:**
 
 
• During Dashain, public spaces, temples, and homes are adorned with decorations, while Tihar features extensive use of **oil lamps and rangolis**.
 
• Both festivals are declared public holidays in Nepal, ensuring nationwide participation.
